# ui::ControlDescription

Header: `winui/ui/ControlHeader.hpp`.

The `description` an input control ([TextBox](../controls/text-box.md#uitextbox), [PasswordBox](../controls/password-box.md#uipasswordbox), [NumberBox](../controls/number-box.md#uinumberbox), [AutoSuggestBox](../controls/auto-suggest-box.md#uiautosuggestbox), [RichEditBox](../controls/rich-edit-box.md#uiricheditbox), [ComboBox](../controls/combo-box.md#uicombobox)) carries under itself. It draws wrapping text in the secondary text color and takes no room while empty. While the control's [`error`](#error) is set, the error shows in its place in the critical color.

It works like [ControlHeader](control-header.md), below the control instead of above it. [measure()](#measure) it along with the header, take its height out of the room the control measures in, and [arrange()](#arrange) it off the bottom of the bounds.

Example: 
```cpp
class DescribedThing : public ui::Element
{
    ui::Size measure_override(ui::Size available, const ui::MeasureContext& context) const override
    {
        const ui::Size header      = header_.measure(available.width, context);
        const ui::Size description = description_.measure(available.width, context);
        const ui::Size under_head  = ui::ControlHeader::below(available, header);
        const ui::Size room        = ui::ControlHeader::below(under_head, description);
        const ui::Size body{120.0f, std::min(room.height, 32.0f)};
        return ui::ControlHeader::above(ui::ControlHeader::above(body, header), description);
    }
    void arrange_override(const ui::Rect&, const ui::ArrangeContext&) override
    {
        header_.arrange(*this);
        description_.arrange(*this); // bounds() is now the body's rect
    }

    ui::ControlHeader      header_{4.0f};
    ui::ControlDescription description_;
};
```

## text

```cpp
const std::string& text() const
```

The description text; empty (the default) collapses it entirely.

## set_text

```cpp
bool set_text(std::string text)
```

Returns whether the text changed, so the caller knows to mark itself dirty for layout and visuals.

## error

```cpp
const std::string& error() const
```

The error text; empty (the default) shows the description.

## set_error

```cpp
bool set_error(std::string error)
```

Returns whether the error changed, so the caller knows to mark itself dirty.

## has_error

```cpp
bool has_error() const
```

True while an error is set.

## shown

```cpp
const std::string& shown() const
```

What shows under the control: the error while one is set, else the description.

## empty

```cpp
bool empty() const
```

True while there is nothing to show: it takes no room and draws nothing.

## measure

```cpp
Size measure(float available_width, const MeasureContext& context) const
```

The room the description takes under the control, in DIPs. Zero when empty. It wraps at `available_width` when that is bounded (> 0).

## arrange

```cpp
void arrange(Element& control)
```

Takes the description (as last measured) off the bottom of `control`'s bounds(), which are left as the control's own rect. Call it from the control's arrange_override(). A no-op while empty.

## render

```cpp
void render(Renderer& renderer, const Theme& theme, bool enabled) const
```

Draws the description where [arrange()](#arrange) put it, in the secondary text color (the disabled color while the control is disabled), or the error in the critical color.
